touches.text: exemptions: the declared list of places a check skips something, each with its reason. WHY: a skip with no written reason is a hole nobody can see.
import_sieve: one parse of every .py into an import graph; what reaches what. WHY: enforces "only the proxy reaches the host/database" and RULE 1 by physics. USERS: CodeMother, the inference proxy.

The RULE 1 check is a path check: code inside device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo (anything not under cairn.devices.bar), except a tool foo publishes (cairn.devices.foo.tools.<x>, its charter saying published_by_device). Inside one device there is one owner, so nothing is checked there. A charter's public_interface describes what the component offers (modules, functions, bus verbs, commands); the check does not read it. Akien 2026-11-09 (Q#77): "wouldn't it be easier (for the python code anyway) to see if the imports do not include other device paths?"

The only way to the inference host; anything that goes around it is an error. WHY: its two points are to find the cheapest model powerful enough for each request, and to train the graph trees on the results.

You said 2026-10-17 it houses the gates "only because we had to have some place to put them". Is `clear` a harbor verb to add here, or should a crossing reach the gate through another door?

Route also moves a domain's preferred models ahead of cheaper ones (route.py:301, since 2026-08-28), and nothing here names that. Does the walk order read "a domain's preferred models first, then cheapest", or does the preference go?
